children: HDFC Bank shares came under pressure after the previous session’s gains, with the stock tracking broader weakness in financials amid cautious market sentiment

HDFC Bank shares slipped below the Rs 716 mark on Thursday, extending volatility in the stock after it had gained in the previous session following developments around the lender’s chief executive succession process.
The stock touched an intraday low below Rs 716 before recovering some ground. It eventually closed at Rs 713, down 1.3 per cent, while the broader Sensex ended almost flat.

HDFC Bank had risen around 3 per cent in the previous session after the bank submitted two candidates to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for the position of managing director and chief executive officer. The lender has not publicly disclosed the names of the candidates.
The succession process remains a key factor for investors as Sashidhar Jagdishan’s second term as HDFC Bank’s MD and CEO is scheduled to end in October 2026.

The bank’s board has proposed changes to its leadership structure, including the appointment of V Srinivasa Rangan as a whole-time director and Chief Credit Officer Jimmy Tata as a whole-time director. It has also proposed creating a fourth whole-time director position for the incoming CEO.
The RBI’s decision on the candidates is now being closely watched by the market. HDFC Bank’s shares had gained on Tuesday after the lender submitted the names, before trading lower on Thursday.

The stock’s movement also came against a cautious backdrop for Indian equities. Markets were responding to the US Federal Reserve’s 25-basis-point rate increase and signals that another hike could be possible, while elevated crude oil prices and foreign fund selling continued to weigh on sentiment.

HDFC Bank has also faced sustained pressure this year. Market data showed the stock remained significantly below its 52-week high, with its decline during 2026 attracting increased attention from investors and analysts.
The immediate focus for the stock remains the RBI’s decision on the bank’s proposed CEO candidates and the broader outlook for the lender amid changing global interest-rate conditions.
